description: Find which rivals, public or private, are gaining ground on a company: launches, pricing, hiring, funding and customer wins, each dated and sourced. Alpha on share shifts.
suggested_questions: Which competitors are gaining ground on Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) in telehealth weight loss since 2026-03-01? Return up to 25 dated signals.
Which competitors, including private ones, are gaining ground on Figma (FIG) since 2026-05-01? Return up to 25 dated signals.
Which competitors are gaining ground on Snowflake (SNOW) since 2026-04-01? Return up to 25 dated signals.
skill:
Where competitor momentum shows:
- Product and pricing: competitors' product pages, changelogs, release notes, pricing pages and their archived copies
  at web.archive.org.
- Hiring: careers pages and ATS boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday) with open-role counts by function and
  region; a count compared with an earlier archived count is a growth signal.
- Funding and deals: company press releases, SEC Form D filings for private raises, investor announcements, funding
  news in trade and business press.
- Customers: customer case studies and logo pages, customers' own announcements, public-sector awards on USAspending,
  app store rank and review counts.
- Expansion: new office, region or country pages, local registry filings, partnership and marketplace listings.
- Public competitors: their earnings releases and filings for segment growth they report.

What terms mean:
- threat_to_company: rising (the signal points to the competitor taking customers, pricing room or talent from the
  company in the request), falling, neutral, cannot_verify.
- metric_value is the number the page prints, with its unit; growth rates are only those the page states.

Where the alpha is: private competitors leave no earnings report, so their hiring, pricing and customer pages are the
only early read on share shifts the public company will report later.

Pitfalls: job posts are reposted and left open; a funding headline is not traction; a launch announcement is not
availability; an aggregator's headcount is not a careers page count.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: One row per dated competitor signal.

items.description: One row per dated competitor signal.

metric_value.description: Number the page prints, as a plain number. Null if none.

metric_unit.description: Unit of metric_value, e.g. open roles, USD millions.

threat_to_company.description: Direction for the company in the request.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.
